items.title: 30.6 Determining the Possible Structure of a Molecule from 1H NMR

source_refs.note: Topic 30.6 with Example 30.2 (PDF 211); the spectrum is redrawn as a sketch. The printed 'No. of peaks = No of protons' and the 3.9 ppm 'doublet' are corrected in warnings.

blocks.text: The structure of an unknown compound can be deduced from its 1H NMR spectrum by putting the information together like a puzzle.

items: Count the peaks: the number of peaks is the number of proton environments.
Use the chemical shift of each peak to identify functional groups (Table 30.1).
Use the peak areas to find the number of hydrogen atoms in each environment.
Analyse the splitting: number of sub-peaks = n + 1, so n (adjacent protons) = number of sub-peaks - 1.
Combine the information to assemble the structure.

blocks.title: Peaks count environments, not protons
blocks.text: The book writes 'No. of peaks = No. of protons'. The number of peaks equals the number of proton environments; the number of protons in each environment comes from the peak areas.

blocks.caption: Example 30.2: the 1H NMR spectrum of an ester
rows: -CH2- next to an electronegative O atom

blocks.text: Combining the three signals gives the structure CH3-CO-O-CH2-CH3, ethyl ethanoate.

blocks.title: The 3.9 ppm signal is a quartet
blocks.text: The book's table calls the 3.9 ppm signal a doublet with 2 - 1 = 1 neighbour. The CH2 next to oxygen has three neighbouring protons (the CH3), so it is a quartet: 4 - 1 = 3.

blocks.alt: Top: a sketch of the spectrum from the book's values, a quartet at 3.9 ppm (2H), a singlet at 2.2 ppm (3H) and a triplet at 1.3 ppm (3H). Bottom: the structure CH3-CO-O-CH2-CH3, with notes matching each signal to its group.
blocks.caption: Deducing the structure of ethyl ethanoate from its 1H NMR spectrum (original sketch for Example 30.2).
blocks.long_description: The singlet at 2.2 ppm is a CH3 next to C=O with no neighbouring H. The quartet at 3.9 ppm and the triplet at 1.3 ppm together are an ethyl group, with its CH2 next to oxygen. Joining these gives the ester CH3COOCH2CH3.

blocks.prompt: An ethyl group (-CH2CH3) gives what pair of signals?
blocks.explanation: A quartet (CH2, area 2, split by the CH3) and a triplet (CH3, area 3, split by the CH2).

items: Peaks = environments; shifts = groups; areas = numbers of H; splitting = neighbours.
